LESSON: DRESSING ENVIRONMENT

Grade: PP1
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: SOCIAL
Topic 1.5: Dressing ENVIRONMENT

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Dressing ENVIRONMENT. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What clothes do people wear ENVIRONMENT learners should be able to; identify clothes worn at at home?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Dressing ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Dressing ENVIRONMENT from Kenya
3. practise Dressing ENVIRONMENT in clear steps
4. apply Dressing ENVIRONMENT in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DRESSING ENVIRONMENT
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Dressing ENVIRONMENT helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: DRESSING ENVIRONMENT
Study Dressing ENVIRONMENT like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Dressing ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Dressing ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Dressing ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Dressing ENVIRONMENT” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Dressing ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Dressing ENVIRONMENT from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Dressing ENVIRONMENT from Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Dressing ENVIRONMENT from Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Dressing ENVIRONMENT matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Dressing ENVIRONMENT from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Dressing ENVIRONMENT in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Dressing ENVIRONMENT in clear steps. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Dressing ENVIRONMENT in clear steps.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Dressing ENVIRONMENT this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Dressing ENVIRONMENT in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Dressing ENVIRONMENT in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Dressing ENVIRONMENT in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Dressing ENVIRONMENT in one real-life situation this week.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Dressing ENVIRONMENT” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Dressing ENVIRONMENT in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Dressing ENVIRONMENT is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Dressing ENVIRONMENT” around your school. (skill: explain what Dressing ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Say why Dressing ENVIRONMENT matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Dressing ENVIRONMENT from Kenya)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Dressing ENVIRONMENT this week. (skill: practise Dressing ENVIRONMENT in clear steps)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Dressing ENVIRONMENT” around your school. (skill: apply Dressing ENVIRONMENT in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Dressing ENVIRONMENT to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Dressing ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Dressing ENVIRONMENT from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Dressing ENVIRONMENT in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Dressing ENVIRONMENT from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Dressing ENVIRONMENT: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Dressing ENVIRONMENT?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What clothes do people wear ENVIRONMENT learners should be able to; identify clothes worn at at home?
2. What clothes do you wear at ( 10 Lessons) different occasions, • Learners are guided in school?
3. What clothes do you wear at occasions. during different occasions. different occasions?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Dressing ENVIRONMENT means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Dressing ENVIRONMENT means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Dressing ENVIRONMENT from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
